# Cookie without Secure or HttpOnly (Node.js)

`qualor:js/insecure-cookie` · Security hotspot · Severity: Low · [CWE-614](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/614.html), [CWE-1004](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1004.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A02_2025-Security_Misconfiguration/), [A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/)

> **Security hotspot.** This rule asks for a review: it marks code that is often safe and
> sometimes not, and a person decides which. A hotspot never fails the quality gate.

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Cookies set without the `Secure` flag, without the `HttpOnly` flag, or without both, by the
documented defaults of each library:

- Express `res.cookie(name, value, options)` and Fastify's `reply.setCookie()` (or
  `reply.cookie()`) from `@fastify/cookie`, where both flags are off unless the options turn them
  on; the options may be written in the call or built in a variable first (with `@fastify/cookie`'s
  `parseOptions` setting both flags for every cookie, the calls are not reported);
- `express-session`, whose session cookie has `HttpOnly` but no `Secure` unless
  `cookie.secure` is set;
- `cookie-session` with an explicit `secure: false` or `httpOnly: false`;
- Next.js `cookies().set()` (from `next/headers`) and `response.cookies.set()` on a
  `NextResponse`, which set neither flag by default.

A flag counts as set when it is given any value but `false`, also later in the code before the
cookie is set (`sess.cookie.secure = true` in a production branch). Cookies that are being
deleted (an expiry at the epoch, `maxAge: 0`, or an empty Next.js value) are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Without `Secure`, the browser also sends the cookie over plain HTTP, where anyone on the network
path can read it. Without `HttpOnly`, every script on the page can read it, including a script
injected through a cross-site scripting flaw. For a session id or a token, either gap is enough to
take over the user's session.

Not every cookie holds a secret: a theme or a language preference may well go without these
flags. That is why this is a hotspot: check what the cookie holds.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** a session cookie without `Secure` and `HttpOnly`.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

app.post('/login', (req, res) => {
  const token = createSessionToken();
  res.cookie('session', token, { maxAge: 3600000 });
  res.redirect('/');
});

function createSessionToken() {
  return 'generated';
}
```

**Compliant:** both flags set (and `sameSite`, which limits cross-site requests).

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

app.post('/login', (req, res) => {
  const token = createSessionToken();
  res.cookie('session', token, { maxAge: 3600000, secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' });
  res.redirect('/');
});

function createSessionToken() {
  return 'generated';
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- For a session id, a token or other sensitive data, set both flags: `{ secure: true, httpOnly:
  true }` in the cookie options (Express, Fastify, Next.js), `cookie: { secure: true }` for
  `express-session` (behind a proxy, with `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`), and leave
  `cookie-session`'s defaults on.
- Consider `sameSite: 'lax'` (or `'strict'`) as well.
- If the cookie holds nothing sensitive and scripts must read it, the code can stay as it is.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- `express-session`
- `cookie-session`
- Fastify
- Next.js

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Cookie options passed in as a parameter or imported from another module are not checked, nor
  are `Set-Cookie` headers written by hand.
- Options built in a variable are followed from an object that holds a cookie option (`maxAge`,
  `path`, `httpOnly`, ...; `secret` for `express-session`): an empty object filled in later is not
  checked.
- An option set to `false` later in the code (`opts.secure = false`) counts as a decided value
  and is not reported.
- A response object is recognised by its name (`res`, `response`, `reply`, ...).
- `@fastify/cookie`'s `parseOptions` count only when they set both flags; then a flag set to `false`
  in a single call is missed.
- A cookie deleted with an expiry in the past other than the epoch is reported.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
